quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull to the side of the road and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Roads become slippery when rain starts, especially in the center of the lane. It is safest to ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest chance of conflict between you and other road users?

options.text: At intersections.
On open highways.
On rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other traffic. Always use extra caution when entering or riding through an intersection.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding. What does SEE stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: Experienced riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions while riding. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane for safety. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases the risk of a crash. Riding on the far side may make the driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and only proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: If bright sunlight makes it hard for drivers to see your turn signals, what should you do?

options.text: Continue to use the mechanical turn signals.
Honk your horn to tell other drivers you are turning.
Use hand signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use hand signals.
questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your turn signals hard to see. It is very important to clearly tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols or words. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you position yourself in your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. This is the safest position. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side can cause the driver to return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: When should you use hearing protection?

options.text: It is not needed if you wear a helmet.
Only on long trips.
On all rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all rides.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Always wear hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: What does it feel like if your front tire goes flat?

options.text: Heavy.
Loose.
Soft.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy.
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop riding and check your tires right away.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface?

options.text: A gravel road
A paved driveway
Dry pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: A gravel road
questions.explanation: Wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement can be slippery. Gravel roads, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers also have poor traction.

questions.question: When riding near a truck:

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
You should focus on riding and not worry about the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding in the blind spots of trucks. Remember: if you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: A passenger on a motorcycle should:

options.text: Put their feet on the ground when the motorcycle is stopped.
Not ride without a back rest.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator.
questions.explanation: A passenger should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: An ideal lane position should:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Invite others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from other drivers' blind spots, wind blasts, and hazards. It also discourages others from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: Motorcycles may pass on the right:

options.text: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
By riding on the shoulder of the road.
By riding on the grass, if it is level.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right only if there is at least eight feet of clear pavement to the right of the vehicle being passed. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Which is not important when choosing riding clothes?

options.text: The clothing protects you from heat and cold.
The clothing makes you more visible to others.
The clothing does not leave weird tan lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: The clothing does not leave weird tan lines.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you in a crash and make you more visible. They also protect you from heat, cold, road debris, and the hot and moving parts of the motorcycle.

questions.question: The safest part of the lane:

options.text: Is always the left portion of the lane.
Is always the right portion of the lane.
Changes depending on the situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes depending on the situation.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best or always worst. Change your lane position based on the conditions.

questions.question: The center portion of the lane:

options.text: Should always be avoided.
Has oil and grease but usually provides enough grip for safe riding.
Does not let other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has oil and grease but usually provides enough grip for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars build up in the center of each lane. This area usually still has enough grip for safe riding, unless it is raining.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield can protect you from:

options.text: Noise.
Dust.
Glare.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dust.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your face in a crash. It also protects against pebbles, wind, dust, dirt, rain, and insects.

questions.question: To shift up to a higher gear, you must:

options.text: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift.
Place your foot over the shift lever and push.
Use your thumb to move the lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift.
questions.explanation: To shift up, place your foot under the shift lever and lift.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what happens if two vehicles arrive at the same time?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to signal the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns drivers that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, how should the following distance change?

options.text: Increase.
Decrease.
Stay the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle towing a trailer should increase its following distance. The trailer adds weight, so the motorcycle needs more distance to stop safely.

questions.question: If another driver makes eye contact with you, what does it mean?

options.text: You know they have seen you.
Eye contact does not always mean they have actually seen you.
They will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Eye contact does not always mean they have actually seen you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume a driver has seen you just because they made eye contact. Drivers can look directly at a motorcycle and still not notice it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that go slower than 25 mph, such as farm equipment or horse-drawn vehicles.
